title: The Surprisingly Specific Origin of 'Hello, World!'
explainer: The convention of writing a trivial 'hello, world' program as the first test on a new language or platform is usually traced to Brian Kernighan's early-1970s Bell Labs tutorial on the B programming language, years before it was popularized by Kernighan and Ritchie's book on C. There was no technical reason the phrase had to be 'hello, world' - it stuck purely as inherited habit, the same habit you're about to repeat across several unrelated platforms in this lesson. It's a small reminder that programming carries forward plenty of pure convention, not just necessity.
